transcript:
[00:00:00] Liam Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Liam from Redwood, our AE. Uh, quick roll call?
[00:00:06] Daniel Ruiz: Hi, Daniel here, CTO at Apex.
[00:00:08] Priya Nair: Priya, Head of Platform.
[00:00:10] Samir Khan: Samir, S R E.
[00:00:12] Aisha Gomez: Aisha, product.
[00:00:14] Maya Patel: Hey, Maya from Redwood SE team.
[00:00:16] Liam Chen: Cool. Agenda: reliability, incident tolerance, fallbacks, multi-region routing, and SLA expectations. We'll spend most time on architecture and failure modes. If we need to, we can schedule a follow up deep-dive. Sound good?
[00:00:28] Daniel Ruiz: Yep. High level — we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private for our user-facing payments fraud decisioning microservice. Latency SLO is 50-100ms p95 depending on region. If region out, we need graceful degradation and a fallback path.
[00:00:42] Priya Nair: Also strict compliance in EU, and we need audit logs and K M S integration.
[00:00:46] Liam Chen: Great, thanks. Maya, do you want to start with how Redwood handles multi-region fallbacks?
[00:00:51] Maya Patel: Sure. At a high level we support routing policies by latency, cost, and region. For hosted customers we have multi-region endpoints — the control plane can route to nearest region by geo or latency probe, and we support automatic fallback to another region or to a cheaper model variant if capacity constrained. For dedicated or private, we can configure cross-region failover via smart routing or customer-managed DNS + health checks.
[00:01:14] Samir Khan: How do you do the routing — DNS TTL or anycast or internal routing? We can't rely on long DNS TTLs for failover.
[00:01:20] Maya Patel: Good question. For hosted we use a combination: anycast at the edge + health-based routing in front of our control plane. TTLs are small, and we do active health probes. For dedicated, if it's in our cloud pool, we can push BGP/anycast changes; for private/VPC deployments we provide a control-plane agent that can flip routes and update internal LB configs. There's some coordination needed with your network team for private.
[00:01:40] Daniel Ruiz: If a region goes down, what's the client-side behavior? Do you surface an error or does Redwood handle retries?
[00:01:46] Maya Patel: By default the SDK will retry on a 5xx and re-route based on the policy you pick. You can enable automatic cross-region fallback so the SDK will transparently hit a secondary region. We also offer a mode where you get explicit error codes so your app can implement tiered fallbacks (e.g., local model -> regional model -> cached results).
[00:02:03] Priya Nair: Is there a cache at the prefix/K V layer that can be used to handle short outages?
[00:02:08] Maya Patel: Yes, we have prefix and KV caching. For chat/generation we maintain a KV cache for session tokens; you can enable short TTL prefix caching — it's meant for a few seconds to a couple minutes to smooth spikes. For a full region outage, cached responses help for identical requests, but for decisioning you probably want deterministic fallback models.
[00:02:25] Aisha Gomez: Deterministic how? Give an example.
[00:02:28] Maya Patel: Example: primary is a large model in eu-west1, fallback is a quantized variant or smaller model in eu-west2 or us-central with known quality delta. Or fallback could be a local ruleset in your service that uses last-known-good ML thresholds.
[00:02:42] Samir Khan: Latency — if we route from EU to US as fallback, that'll blow our SLOs for p95.
[00:02:47] Liam Chen: Right, that's why we commonly recommend a multi-tier: regional primary, regional smaller fallback, then remote global fallback. For payments you can set policy to prefer local, then regional, and fail open/closed depending on the endpoint semantics.
[00:03:03] Daniel Ruiz: About SLAs — what's Redwood's p95 SLA and credits if you miss?
[00:03:09] Liam Chen: For hosted API we publish best-effort numbers and for enterprise customers we offer SLA-backed latency and uptime in Dedicated with SLOs in contract. Typical uptime SLA is 99.95% for Dedicated/Reserved pools; Hosted has higher variability unless you buy premium support. Credits are specified in the contract — usually proportional to downtime beyond the SLO.
[00:03:29] Priya Nair: For private deployments, do you provide the control plane and we own the infra — what's the SLA surface then?
[00:03:36] Maya Patel: For Private, the customer usually owns compute and network. We provide the control plane either hosted or as a customer-managed appliance. SLA then is a hybrid — Redwood guarantees the control plane uptime if hosted, but for on-prem compute we assist with runbooks; the contractual uptime model is adjusted and we include remediation assistance.
[00:03:52] Samir Khan: Ok. What about live failover testing? How invasive is it?
[00:03:56] Maya Patel: We can run chaos/failover tests with a canary schedule. For hosted, we can simulate region failover in a sandbox. For Dedicated we can orchestrate test failovers during a maintenance window. For Private, we provide a test harness and recommend a DR playbook. We'll share the benchmark spreadsheet and a suggested test harness.
[00:04:14] Liam Chen: We'll add that to next steps. Real quick on data residency — you mentioned EU compliance, Priya.
[00:04:19] Priya Nair: Yes, all payment decision logs must remain in EU per our policy and we need audit logs for 3 years.
[00:04:24] Maya Patel: Redwood supports region pinning for storage and model execution; logs can be routed to your K M S and audit trail. For hosted, we provide regional data residency options and can integrate with your K M S for key control. For Dedicated/Private, keys live in your K M S or H S M.
[00:04:38] Daniel Ruiz: Does hosted let us bring-your-own K M S?
[00:04:41] Maya Patel: Yes, for enterprise hosted customers we support BYOK via customer-managed keys in the cloud K M S or H S M through our integration layer.
[00:04:47] Samir Khan: In case of a partial outage, how do you ensure in-flight requests don't get lost or double-charged?
[00:04:54] Maya Patel: We maintain idempotency keys at the request layer and the control plane tracks request status. If a region cut occurs we can either retry with idempotency or return a clear status so the client can decide. Billing is tied to successfully processed tokens, and we have logs to reconcile. There have been a few imperfect transcriptions in logs historically, but we keep an audit trail.
[00:05:14] Aisha Gomez: You mentioned model variant fallback — how do you quantify quality loss?
[00:05:19] Maya Patel: We run model A/Bs and maintain quality deltas in the model catalog. For each variant we provide expected latency/cost/quality metrics for your workload. We can run a small eval run on your sample prompts to estimate regressions.
[00:05:32] Liam Chen: We also have Redwood Optimize which suggests quantization and batching to hit latency goals. For decisioning, often teams use a smaller quantized model as the failover to keep latency within SLO.
[00:05:43] Priya Nair: For logging and audits, can we stream logs to our SIEM?
[00:05:47] Maya Patel: Yes, we support log streaming to your SIEM via secure forwarder or direct API. We also offer SSO/SAML and SCIM for provisioning.
[00:05:55] Daniel Ruiz: Network egress — if we fall back to US region, are there egress costs back to EU and does Redwood charge for cross-region traffic?
[00:06:02] Liam Chen: Cross-region egress is billable in Dedicated/private setups and we include estimated egress in the pricing model. For hosted we try to absorb some costs but large volumes are passed through per contract. We'll include region egress estimates in the pricing doc.
[00:06:16] Samir Khan: For private deployments in our VPC, how does the control plane communicate? Is it a persistent websocket?
[00:06:21] Maya Patel: Our control plane agent establishes outbound TLS connections to the Redwood control plane over port 443 — no inbound ports needed. For lower trust setups we can use a VPN or direct interconnect. The agent handles heartbeat and health for failover actions.
[00:06:36] Priya Nair: Any compliance artifacts you can share now?
[00:06:39] Liam Chen: We'll send SOC 2 and ISO attestation docs — and a security whitepaper for Private deployments. Link in notes: https://redwood.example/share/security-whitepaper (we'll actually share post-call).
[00:06:49] Daniel Ruiz: Ok, concrete concern: can we avoid any single region dependency? We have regulatory preference for primary in EU but backup outside EU only for non-PII. How do you support partial fallbacks?
[00:07:00] Maya Patel: You can configure per-route policies to restrict certain data/requests to region-only. For non-PII you can enable cross-region fallback. For PII we recommend hybrid approach: keep model execution and logs in EU, and if EU fails, fall back to a ruleset or degraded model that runs locally. We can label routes and enforce routing via policy.
[00:07:19] Samir Khan: About metrics and observability: do you expose per-token latency per-region and per-model?
[00:07:25] Maya Patel: Yes, Redwood Console provides per-model/per-route dashboards with p50/p95/p99, token count, and error rates. We also emit traces for each request that you can ingest into your tracing system.
[00:07:36] Aisha Gomez: Will you help with runbook creation?
[00:07:38] Maya Patel: Absolutely. For enterprise customers we collaborate on DR runbooks and playbooks for failover, test plans, and rollback. We'll include sample runbooks in the follow-up package.
[00:07:48] Liam Chen: Any other questions on routing and fallback?
[00:07:50] Daniel Ruiz: One more — how long does a cross-model rollout take if we need to switch primary model after an incident?
[00:07:56] Maya Patel: Rollouts can be near-instant at the control plane level — you can flip alias to another model or do canary percent-based rollouts. Actual latency depends on warm-up/K V cache population; cold starts may add some ms. We recommend warming caches and preloading KV for sessions.
[00:08:12] Priya Nair: Are there tools to simulate cold start or cache warming?
[00:08:15] Maya Patel: Yes, our benchmark harness supports simulated traffic to warm model caches and preload KV prefixes. We'll attach the harness.
[00:08:23] Liam Chen: Great. Let's do a quick recap and next steps.
[00:08:26] Liam Chen: Recap: Apex needs EU primary with audit logs, BYOK, 3-year audit retention, p95 50-100ms target, and multi-tier fallback policy that avoids sending PII outside EU. Redwood to send pricing, region egress estimates, security docs, benchmark workbook, test harness, and schedule a technical deep-dive.
[00:08:44] Daniel Ruiz: Sounds right. Samir, anything else?
[00:08:46] Samir Khan: We'll provide traffic histograms and RTO targets, and want a window to run chaos tests.
[00:08:51] Liam Chen: Perfect. We'll get items out this week. Thanks for your time.
[00:08:55] Priya Nair: Thanks.
[00:08:56] Aisha Gomez: Thanks, bye.
[00:08:58] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. Bye.

Summary:
- Discovery call focused on reliability, multi-region fallbacks, and SLA differences between Hosted / Dedicated / Private.
- Redwood outlined routing strategies (anycast + health routing), SDK retry behaviors, prefix/KV caching, model variant fallbacks, and tools for chaos/failover testing.
- Compliance and data residency (EU) are primary constraints; BYOK and audit log retention discussed.
- Next steps include pricing, benchmark workbook, security docs, and a technical deep-dive.
